content.text:
The flashing windows come from how the Windows release build is set up, and nothing in the code turns them off.

**Why it happens**

- `src/main.rs:2` builds release versions with `windows_subsystem = "windows"`. That makes Suspense a GUI app with no console of its own.
- On Windows, when a process with no console starts a console program, the OS gives that program a new console window. The window shows for as long as the program runs and closes when it exits.
- Suspense starts console programs all the time, and about 54 call sites use `std::process::Command::new(...)`:
  - `git` for status polling, the git panel, diffs and task snapshots
  - `piton` for builds, fluency, the LSP and slicing
  - `podman`
  - the harness (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`)
  - `taskkill` and `cmd` for run targets

  The status polling alone keeps a steady stream of windows going.
- None of these call sites set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. `creation_flags` appears nowhere in `src`.
- Debug builds don't use the GUI subsystem, so their child programs share the existing console. That's why this only shows up in the release build.

**The fix**

- Set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x08000000`) on every child process on Windows, using `std::os::windows::process::CommandExt::creation_flags`.
- The clean way is a single helper, say `crate::process::command(program) -> Command`, that applies the flag behind `#[cfg(windows)]`. Then replace every `Command::new` with it, including the existing builders `container::podman_command` and `harness::one_off_command`.
- Output can still be captured with the flag set, because stdout and stderr are piped.
- One exception: the Podman login runs under a pseudo-terminal and must keep working. That's ConPTY on Windows, which doesn't open a visible window anyway.

The spec says nothing about this (I searched the reference), so the next agent can bring the flashing back. Use a Chain prompt so the rule goes into the spec and the code follows from it:

```suspense-prompt chain
On Windows, no program the application runs opens a window of its own. Every child process it starts on the host, git, piton (builds, slicing, its language server, fluency), podman, the harness and its one-off runs, a run target's shell, and the commands that stop a process, is started without a console window, so nothing flashes on screen while the application works, in a release build as in a development one. What these programs print is still read as ever. The login view's command, run under a pseudo-terminal, still works as the ContainerEnvironmentScope says.

Say this once, in the ApplicationScope, and give the reason: a release build on Windows is a GUI application with no console, so Windows gives every console program it starts a window of its own unless told not to.

In the code, start every child process through one shared helper that sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows (std::os::windows::process::CommandExt::creation_flags, 0x08000000) and does nothing elsewhere, and replace every direct std::process::Command::new in src with it, including container::podman_command and harness::one_off_command. Tests may keep using Command directly.
```
